title: Someone Measures, Sobbing…
text:
Someone measures, sobbing,
+
+the breadth of dawn.
+
+Someone stabs the pillow
+
+in search of their impossible
+
+resting place.
editorial_note: The anonymous alguien remains ungendered; dawn becomes measurable only through sobbing, and rest an impossible place sought through violence.

title: Sing, My Wounded One…
text:
Sing, my wounded one
+
+Cervantes
+
+
+though it is late, it is night,
+
+and you cannot.
+
+
+Sing as though nothing were happening.
+
+
+Nothing happens
editorial_note: The isolated Cervantes is preserved as it appears in the source, between address and impossibility; the final nada turns consolation into literal nothingness.

title: Poem
text:
You choose the place of the wound
+
+where we speak our silence.
+
+You make of my life
+
+this ceremony too pure.
editorial_note: The lovers speak not in but their silence; the wound becomes a chosen site and life a ceremony whose excessive purity is itself dangerous.

title: In an Ancient Autumn
text:
What is the name called?
+
+
+A color like a coffin, a transparency you will not cross.
+
+
+And how is it possible not to know so much?
editorial_note: The apparent tautology of naming and the paradoxical abundance of not-knowing remain intact; transparency is rendered as an uncrossable substance.

title: Figures and Silences
text:
Clenched hands confine me to exile.
+
+Help me not to ask for help.
+
+They want to nightfall me, they are going to die me.
+
+Help me not to ask for help.
editorial_note: Pizarnik’s transitive anochecer and morir are recreated as nightfall me and die me; grammatical violence enacts the threatened violence against the speaker.

title: Insist on Your Embrace…
text:
Insist on your embrace,
+
+redouble your fury,
+
+create a space of insults
+
+between I and the mirror,
+
+create a leper woman’s song
+
+between I and the woman I believe myself to be.
editorial_note: The nonstandard entre yo is intentionally carried into between I, keeping the grammatical split between speaker, reflection, and imagined self.

title: Time
text:
I know nothing of childhood
+
+but a luminous fear
+
+and a hand that drags me
+
+to my other shore.
+
+
+My childhood and its scent
+
+of a caressed bird.
editorial_note: Childhood is known only through fear, forced passage, and scent; the other shore remains psychological, mortal, and spatial at once.

title: Invocations
text:
Insist on your embrace,
+
+redouble your fury,
+
+create a space of insults
+
+between I and the mirror,
+
+create a leper woman’s song
+
+between I and the woman I believe myself to be.
editorial_note: This separately hashed witness preserves the reviewed grammatical fracture and invocation while differing from the first-line record only in source spacing.
